blocks.title: Mombasa port clearance process
blocks.body: Mombasa clearance works best when the customs file is prepared before the shipment reaches a pressure point. Kenya Tradex checks the cargo description, consignee details, value basis, permits and final destination so the clearance path matches the shipment instead of forcing every file through the same workflow.
items: Review Bill of Lading, commercial invoice, packing list, IDF and permits before vessel arrival.
Check HS code, customs value, duty exposure and inspection risk early to reduce avoidable delays.
Coordinate customs entry, inspection handling, port release, storage decisions and onward delivery.
Plan regional transit movement where cargo is not destined for Kenya.

blocks.title: Documents and decisions to prepare early
blocks.body: The invoice, packing list and Bill of Lading should describe the same cargo, consignee and shipment terms. Small mismatches can trigger avoidable clarification before release.
paragraphs: HS code, customs value, IDF status and permits should be reviewed before arrival, especially for regulated cargo, machinery, food items, electronics and mixed consignments.
Local delivery, bonded storage, Nairobi movement or regional transit should be selected early so transport, storage and customs requirements do not collide after release.

Duty and agency checks: HS code, customs value, IDF status and permits should be reviewed before arrival, especially for regulated cargo, machinery, food items, electronics and mixed consignments.

blocks.title: Common Mombasa clearance risks
items: Vessel arrives before the importer has shared complete cargo documents.
Product descriptions are too general for confident tariff classification or permit review.
Cargo is selected for inspection but the importer, transporter or warehouse plan is not ready.
Transit cargo is cleared as a port file before the bond, route and final destination requirements are aligned.

faq.question: When should I start customs clearance for cargo arriving at Mombasa Port?
faq.answer: Start before vessel arrival where possible. Kenya Tradex reviews the Bill of Lading, commercial invoice, packing list, IDF, permits and consignee details early so duty exposure, inspection risk and document gaps are visible before storage or demurrage costs build up.

faq.question: Can Mombasa clearance support transit cargo to Uganda, Rwanda, DRC or South Sudan?
faq.answer: Yes. Cargo moving beyond Kenya needs customs clearance planning at Mombasa plus transit bond, road manifest, corridor and border coordination for the destination country.

faq.question: What commonly delays cargo release at Mombasa?
faq.answer: Common delays include incomplete invoices, mismatched consignee details, unclear product descriptions, missing permits, HS code questions, valuation queries, inspection selection and late transport or warehouse arrangements after release.
